subject: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile
messages:
From: Ellen Park <procurement@edgescale.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: EdgeScale Ops <ops@edgescale.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to an internal approval for a wider pilot, but procurement has one contract-level ask before we greenlight: our workload in us-west has predictable high‑impact burst windows (nightly batch scoring plus end‑of‑month funnels). That pattern raises our risk tolerance for short regional degradations.

Specifically we'd like Redwood to consider the following amendments for the us-west deployment during the 12‑month pilot:
- Allow an uptime floor of 99.5% specifically scoped to us-west (we're asking for flexibility vs the platform-wide SLA).
- In lieu of a stricter availability commitment, provide a monthly "safeguard" allowance: a capped settlement pool (service credit or invoice offset) that EdgeScale can draw from if burst-related unavailability materially impacts job windows.

Our priority is predictable operational impact and a simple mechanism to reconcile missed windows; we prefer a single monthly pool versus complex per-incident calculations. We'd like draft language we can take to legal, plus an estimate of how the safeguard would be sized (nominal $ or token credit) and a proposed cap.

I've attached a short note that summarizes our ask (Edgescale-SLA-ask.pdf). Can we get an initial response by end of next week? We're targetting a May 1 start for the pilot if contract changes are minor.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Procurement, EdgeScale
procurement@edgescale.com

Attachment: Edgescale-SLA-ask.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile

Team — forwarding the EdgeScale ask below. Quick context: they like the platform but want a scoped deviation for one region (us-west) and a simple monthly "safeguard" pool instead of our standard per-incident credit formula.

Key asks to resolve:
- Commercial stance: do we accept a lower regional uptime floor (99.5%) while keeping platform SLA intact elsewhere?
- What is the reasonable size / cap of the monthly safeguard (fixed $ vs % of spend vs token credits)?
- Legal / product: language that operationalizes a region-limited uptime floor and defines what triggers use of the safeguard.

Recommended approach: offer a limited amendment for a 90‑day pilot: 99.9% platform SLA unchanged, but for us-west we can support a pilot-level floor of 99.5% with a monthly safeguard pool equal to 5% of their monthly committed spend or a $15k cap (whichever is lower). We should include auto-failover guidance and a requirement that EdgeScale uses cross‑region routing during burst windows where possible.

Ben/Monica — please weigh in on pricing and CS implications. Aditya — can you provide a short technical note on what operational guarantees we can realistically deliver for region-level commitments and what the fallback behavior will be?

If we can align on numbers, I'll draft a short amendment to push back to them.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_response_framework.docx (DOCX, 22 KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile

Laura — agree with a pilot approach. My quick commercial position:
- Offer: maintain global/overall SLA of 99.95% for their account; provide a scoped us-west floor of 99.5% for the pilot term only (90 days).
- Safeguard: propose a monthly pool equal to the lesser of 5% of billed monthly usage or $12,000 (we can make this tradeable as token credits against invoices).
- Cap: single‑month cap; no cumulative carryover. For transparency, we'll include a simple formula in the amendment.

Rationale: preserves our platform-level commitment while giving EdgeScale a straightforward reconciliation mechanism. If they want the floor permanent post-pilot, we re-evaluate pricing / routing commitments.

I've modeled price impact at a high level — see attached. If legal wants a different trigger condition for using the pool (e.g., impact to job SLA rather than raw uptime), happy to update.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing-impact.csv (CSV, 8 KB)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile

Quick technical read — I like the pilot framing. A few points to make the amendment operationally sound:

1) Scoping the floor: we need the amendment to define "us-west" precisely (region code + cluster ids) so routing and telemetry map to the same metric.
2) Trigger for pool use: recommend we tie the safeguard drawdown to a quantifiable impact (e.g., percentage of scheduled batch runs that failed to complete within window) rather than raw availability. Raw availability can be noisy; the job‑level metric better aligns to their ask.
3) Failover behavior: we can commit to best‑effort cross‑region failover for the pilot but cannot fully guarantee zero added latency. We'll document expected latency delta for cross‑region reroutes and require EdgeScale to enable it in their routing config for pilot eligibility.
4) Monitoring: we'll provide a shared Grafana link and a monthly report showing events that touched the pool.

I've drafted suggested amendment language that captures the above — see attached sample. If legal approves the wording, I recommend a 90‑day pilot start date of May 1 with an automatic review at day 60.

-Aditya
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla_amendment_sample.txt (TXT, 6 KB)

From: Ellen Park <procurement@edgescale.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: EdgeScale Ops <ops@edgescale.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: uptime floor and monthly safeguard for regional burst profile

Laura / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear pilot framing. EdgeScale is prepared to accept the 90‑day pilot with the terms you outlined, subject to a couple of small clarifications:

- We prefer the monthly safeguard cap at $10,000 (rather than $12k) for the pilot to keep internal approvals simple.
- Please include the job‑level trigger language Aditya suggested (percentage of scheduled batch runs impacted) so we have an operational definition.
- We want the pilot to start May 1 and the review at day 60 — that matches our internal timeline.

I've routed the amendment to our legal and will sign via DocuSign once we see the final wording. Attaching a signed cover note to indicate intent.

Happy to have a short 30‑minute sync on Friday if you want to walk the amendment together.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Procurement, EdgeScale
procurement@edgescale.com

Attachment: Edgescale-signed.pdf (PDF, 24 KB)
